title: 面试尾声被问有什么问题想问我们
titleEn: "Any questions for us?" — finishing a job interview strong
scene: 周三上午，你在 Teams 上参加一家医疗服务公司（Torrens Health Group，虚构）业务分析师（BA）岗位的第一轮面试。面试官是团队经理 Sarah 和一位资深 BA。前面的行为题都答完了，Sarah 看了看时间，说：“We've got about ten minutes left — have you got any questions for us?” 这是很多华人求职者最容易“卡壳”或只说 “No, I think you've covered everything” 的环节，其实澳洲面试官很看重这几分钟。
你的目标：① 准备 2–3 个有质量的问题（团队现在最头疼的事、前三个月的期望、混合办公安排）；② 听懂 Sarah 语速快、带口头禅的回答，必要时礼貌追问；③ 最后问清楚下一步流程和时间线（二面、reference check、多久出结果），并得体地收尾道谢。

facts.v: 周三上午 10:00–10:45，Teams 视频面试，最后 10 分钟是提问环节
Sarah（团队经理，hiring manager）+ 一位资深 BA
BA，12 个月合同可续（view to extend），混合办公
周五前出结果 → 二面（案例题）→ reference check

vocab.en: have you got any questions for us?
vocab.zh: 你有什么问题想问我们吗？（面试收尾必问）
vocab.ex: Before we wrap up, have you got any questions for us?
We'll need to wrap up in about ten minutes.

vocab.zh: 典型的一周 / 日常工作内容
vocab.ex: Could you tell me what a typical week looks like in this role?
What's the biggest pain point for the team at the moment?

vocab.en: the first three months / first 90 days
vocab.zh: 入职头三个月（问期望时常用）
vocab.ex: What would success look like in the first three months?

vocab.zh: 一上手就能干活、马上进入状态
vocab.ex: We need someone who can hit the ground running.

vocab.en: hybrid / in the office two days a week
vocab.zh: 混合办公 / 每周两天在办公室
vocab.ex: We're hybrid — most people are in Tuesdays and Thursdays.

vocab.en: a bit all over the place
vocab.ex: To be honest, our processes are a bit all over the place.
There's a fair bit of stakeholder management in this role.

vocab.en: next steps / the process from here
vocab.zh: 下一步 / 接下来的流程
vocab.ex: Could you walk me through the process from here?

vocab.zh: 入围名单 / 第二轮面试
vocab.ex: We'll be shortlisting for a second round next week.
Our recruiter will touch base with you by Friday.

listening.en: Righto, we've got about ten minutes left — have you got any questions for us?
listening.sound: Righto 读作 “rai-toh”（好嘞、那么）；got about 连读成 “go-da-bout”；have you got 弱读成 “hav-ya-got”。
listening.zh: 好，我们还剩大概十分钟——你有什么想问我们的吗？
listening.reply: Yes, I've got a couple, actually. Thanks for asking.

listening.en: Ah, good question. Honestly, it's a bit all over the place at the mo — we're sort of building the plane while we're flying it.
listening.sound: at the mo = at the moment（澳洲口语缩写）；building the plane while we're flying it 是比喻：一边做一边搭流程；sort of 弱读成 “sor-da”。
listening.zh: 嗯，好问题。说实话现在有点乱——我们算是边飞边造飞机。
listening.reply: That sounds like a good opportunity to help set things up properly.

listening.en: We're not expecting you to hit the ground running from day one, but by the three-month mark we'd want you across the claims stuff.
listening.sound: three-month mark 意思是“到三个月的时候”；be across something = 熟悉、掌握某事（澳洲很常用）；claims stuff 里 stuff 指“那一块东西”。
listening.zh: 我们不指望你第一天就上手，但到三个月左右，希望你能熟悉理赔那一块。
listening.reply: That makes sense. Is there any documentation I could read early on?

listening.en: We're hybrid — most of the team's in Tuesdays and Thursdays, but it's pretty flexible, especially with school pick-ups and that.
listening.sound: team's in = team is in（在办公室）；and that 放句尾 = “之类的”；pretty flexible 里 pretty = 挺、相当。
listening.zh: 我们是混合办公——团队大多周二周四来办公室，不过挺灵活的，特别是接孩子之类的情况。
listening.reply: That's really good to hear. I've got two young kids, so that helps a lot.

listening.en: So from here, we're seeing a couple more people this arvo and tomorrow, then Jess from HR'll touch base by Friday arvo either way.
listening.sound: this arvo = 今天下午；HR'll = HR will；either way = 不管结果如何（都会通知你）；seeing people = 面试别人。
listening.zh: 接下来我们今天下午和明天还要面两三个人，然后 HR 的 Jess 会在周五下午前联系你，不管结果怎样。
listening.reply: Great, thanks. And would the second round be in person or online?

listening.en: Anyway, I won't keep you — really appreciate your time today, it's been great chatting.
listening.sound: I won't keep you = 不耽误你了（客气地结束对话）；won't 和 want 要分清：won't 是 “wohnt”，嘴更圆。
listening.zh: 好了，不耽误你了——非常感谢你今天抽时间，聊得很开心。
listening.reply: Thank you both, I really enjoyed it. Looking forward to hearing from you.

speech.topic: 面试最后，我通常会问面试官哪些问题
paragraphs: At the end of most job interviews in Australia, the interviewer asks, "Have you got any questions for us?" When I first moved here, I usually said, "No, I think you've covered everything." Later, a recruiter told me that this is a missed chance. Interviewers want to see that you are curious and that you are thinking about the real job, not just the interview.

Now I always prepare three questions. The first one is about the team: "What's the biggest pain point for the team at the moment?" The answer tells me what problems I would be working on, and it often gives me a chance to share a quick example of how I solved something similar before.

My second question is about expectations: "What would success look like in the first three months?" This shows that I want to do well, and it helps me understand if the role is realistic. If they say they want someone to hit the ground running, I know I need to prepare more before I start.
My third question is about the practical side, like hybrid work or flexibility. As a parent, this matters to me, and I think it's fine to ask politely.

Finally, I always ask about the next steps, for example, "Could you walk me through the process from here?" That way, I don't spend the whole week waiting and guessing. Then I thank them for their time and say I'm looking forward to hearing from them. These last five minutes can really change how they remember you.
speech.zh: 在澳洲面试的最后，面试官几乎都会问“你有什么问题想问我们吗”。我刚来时总说“没有了”，后来招聘顾问告诉我这是错失机会，面试官想看到你有好奇心、在认真想这份工作。现在我总准备三个问题：一是团队现在最头疼的事，这能让我了解要解决什么问题，还能顺势讲讲自己以前的类似经历；二是头三个月怎样算做得好，这体现积极性，也帮我判断岗位是否现实；三是混合办公、灵活性这类实际问题，作为家长我很在意，礼貌地问是没问题的。最后我一定会问接下来的流程，免得一整周干等，然后道谢说期待回复。最后这五分钟真的会改变面试官对你的印象。

patterns.en: What's the biggest ___ for the team at the moment?
patterns.zh: 团队目前最大的___是什么？（challenge / priority / pain point）

patterns.en: What would success look like in the first ___?
patterns.zh: 头___内怎样算做得好？（three months / six months）
能给我讲讲___吗？（the process from here / a typical week）

patterns.en: I really enjoyed ___, and I'm looking forward to ___.

lines.en: Righto, I'm conscious of the time — we've got about ten minutes left. Have you got any questions for us?
lines.zh: 好，我注意一下时间——还剩大概十分钟。你有什么问题想问我们吗？

lines.en: Yes, I've got a couple, actually. Thanks for asking. First, what's the biggest pain point for the team at the moment?
lines.zh: 有的，我有几个问题，谢谢。第一个，团队目前最头疼的问题是什么？

lines.en: Ooh, good one. Um, honestly, it's a bit all over the place at the mo. We've just merged two claims systems, so we're sort of building the plane while we're flying it, if that makes sense.
lines.zh: 哦，好问题。嗯，说实话，现在有点乱。我们刚把两个理赔系统合并，所以有点像边飞边造飞机，你懂我意思吧。

lines.en: Sorry, could you say that last bit again a bit slower? Building the plane…?
lines.zh: 不好意思，最后那句能说慢一点吗？造飞机……？

lines.en: Ha, yeah, sorry — it just means we're fixing the processes while we're still using them. There's no proper documentation yet.
lines.zh: 哈，对，抱歉——意思就是我们一边用这些流程一边在修。目前还没有像样的文档。

lines.en: Got it, thanks. That actually sounds like something I could help with. In my last role, we had to map out the processes after a system upgrade, and I wrote most of the process documents.
lines.zh: 明白了，谢谢。这其实正是我能帮上忙的地方。我上一份工作中，系统升级后我们要梳理流程，大部分流程文档是我写的。

lines.en: Oh, that's handy. Yeah, we'd definitely lean on you for that.
lines.zh: 哦，那挺有用的。是的，这方面我们肯定会很依赖你。

lines.en: My second question is, what would success look like in the first three months?
lines.zh: 我的第二个问题是，头三个月怎样算做得好？

lines.en: Yeah, so we're not expecting you to hit the ground running from day one. But by the three-month mark, we'd want you across the claims stuff, running your own workshops, and sort of owning a couple of the smaller pieces of work.
lines.zh: 嗯，我们不指望你第一天就能完全上手。但到三个月左右，希望你熟悉理赔那一块、能自己主持需求工作坊，并且独立负责几项小一点的工作。

lines.en: Just to confirm, when you say "across the claims stuff", you mean understanding the claims process end to end?
lines.zh: 我确认一下，您说的 across the claims stuff，是指要从头到尾了解理赔流程，对吗？

lines.en: Spot on. Who does what, where it gets stuck, that kind of thing.
lines.zh: 没错。谁负责什么、在哪儿卡住，这类东西。

lines.en: That makes sense. Is there anything I could read early on to get up to speed?
lines.zh: 明白。有没有什么资料我可以提前看，帮助我尽快上手？

lines.en: Not a lot, to be fair, but Priya's put together a bit of a cheat sheet. We'd sit you down with her in the first week.
lines.zh: 说实话不多，不过 Priya 整理了一份速查表。第一周我们会安排你跟她坐下来过一遍。

lines.en: Great. And my last question is more practical. What does the hybrid arrangement look like?
lines.zh: 好的。我最后一个问题比较实际：混合办公是怎么安排的？

lines.en: So we're hybrid — most of the team's in Tuesdays and Thursdays, and the rest is up to you. It's pretty flexible, especially with school pick-ups and that. A few of us have got kids, so we get it.
lines.zh: 我们是混合办公——团队大多周二周四来办公室，其余时间你自己安排。挺灵活的，特别是接孩子之类的。我们好几个人也有孩子，所以都理解。

lines.en: That's really good to hear. I've got two young kids, so that helps a lot.
lines.zh: 听到这个太好了。我有两个小孩，这点很有帮助。

lines.en: Yeah, no worries at all. Anything else?
lines.zh: 嗯，完全没问题。还有别的吗？

lines.en: Just one more thing. Could you walk me through the process from here?
lines.zh: 还有一件事。能给我讲讲接下来的流程吗？

lines.en: Yep, so we're seeing a couple more people this arvo and tomorrow, then Jess from HR'll touch base by Friday arvo either way. If you're through, the second round's a case study — you'd get a bit of a scenario to work through with the team, about an hour.
lines.zh: 好，我们今天下午和明天还要面两三个人，然后 HR 的 Jess 会在周五下午前联系你，不管结果如何。如果你进了下一轮，二面是案例题——给你一个场景，跟团队一起分析，大概一个小时。

lines.en: Sorry, just to check — "either way" means Jess will call me even if I'm not successful?
lines.zh: 不好意思，确认一下——either way 是说即使我没通过，Jess 也会联系我吗？

lines.en: Yep, absolutely. We don't like leaving people hanging.
lines.zh: 对，一定会。我们不喜欢让人干等着。

lines.en: I appreciate that. And would the second round be in person or online?
lines.zh: 非常感谢。那二面是线下还是线上？

lines.en: In person, ideally — we're in the city, on Grenfell Street. But we can do Teams if that's tricky. Then it's just reference checks after that.
lines.zh: 最好是线下——我们在市中心 Grenfell Street。如果不方便也可以用 Teams。之后就只剩背景推荐人核查了。

lines.en: In person is fine. I'll have my referees ready, just in case.
lines.zh: 线下没问题。我会提前准备好推荐人，以防需要。

lines.en: Perfect. Anyway, I won't keep you — really appreciate your time today. It's been great chatting.
lines.zh: 太好了。好了，不耽误你了——非常感谢你今天抽时间，聊得很愉快。

lines.en: Thank you both. I really enjoyed learning more about the team, and I'm looking forward to hearing from Jess. Have a good rest of your day.
lines.zh: 谢谢两位。很高兴更了解了团队，期待 Jess 的消息。祝你们今天剩下的时间愉快。

rescue.en: Sorry, could you say that last bit again a bit slower?
rescue.zh: 不好意思，最后那部分能说慢一点吗？
我确认一下，您的意思是___？

rescue.en: Sorry, I'm not familiar with that expression. What does it mean?
rescue.zh: 抱歉，我不太熟悉那个说法，是什么意思？

rescue.en: Could you spell the name of the HR contact for me?
rescue.zh: 能帮我拼一下 HR 联系人的名字吗？

rescue.en: Would you mind sending the details of the next steps by email?
rescue.zh: 能麻烦把下一步的细节发邮件给我吗？

checklist: 被问 “any questions for us?” 时，我能自然地说出至少 2 个准备好的问题，而不是说 “No, I think you've covered everything”
我能用 “What would success look like in the first three months?” 问岗位期望
我听懂了 at the mo、this arvo、be across something、either way、touch base 这几个说法
听到比喻或俚语（如 building the plane while we're flying it）听不懂时，我能礼貌请对方解释或放慢
我能问清楚下一步流程：谁联系我、什么时候、二面形式
我能用一两句得体的话收尾道谢（I really enjoyed…, looking forward to hearing from…）
